move: hard-cut panels slam, letters punch, wipes, grid explodes, marquee stripes rip
how: Five full-frame colour panels and three images are toggled with autoAlpha sets at hard cut points. 0-17%: a red panel scales up from scaleY 0 (expo.out 0.35s), BLAST letters snap in from scale 3 with stagger 0.06 and the word slowly scales to 1.08. 17%: a sunset image punches in from scale 1.6 with clip-path inset 40%→0 then creeps to 1.12. 32%: a yellow panel wipes xPercent -100→0 (expo.inOut 0.4s), MAKE/NOISE rise masked from yPercent 110 and drift apart ±6%. 52%: an aurora image slams up from yPercent 100, a 3x2 grid of cells pops from scale 0 with back.out(2.5) from centre (each 0.05) and scales to 1.06. 72%: a blue panel drops from yPercent -100 and two rotated marquee stripes rip across (xPercent 45→-15 and -45→15, power2.out 1.2s). 87%: a black panel blooms via clip-path circle 0→80%, logo spins in from rotation -90, name and tagline rise, then the CTA scales to 1.6 and fades, and the black panel is hidden at the last frame.
adapt: Replace the three images, the BLAST / MAKE NOISE / stripe words, the grid cell labels, the panel colours and the closing logo/name; keep the cut points (1.4, 2.6, 4.2, 5.8, 7.0 of 8s) and the sub-0.5s slam durations.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the panels, images, grid and CTA and sets the initial autoAlpha 0 on everything but the first panel; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the cut points as fractions (0.175, 0.325, 0.525, 0.725, 0.875 of D). All #id selectors become el.querySelector; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: relies on many .set autoAlpha cuts; scrubbing backwards across cuts can show stale layers
